summary_paragraph: A woman with sickle cell disease and hepatitis C presented with a six-day history of persistent bilateral knee and left hip pain consistent with a vaso-occlusive crisis. She was managed with IV hydration, IV Dilaudid initially, and transitioned to oral Dilaudid and Toradol as her pain improved. A left hip X-ray showed no avascular necrosis or new structural changes. Her hemoglobin remained stable at her baseline, and she declined transfusion due to prior hepatitis C from transfusions. Folate and B12 levels were normal, with macrocytosis attributed to hydroxyurea. Her home medications, including hydroxyurea, lisinopril, and folate, were continued with dose adjustments at discharge. She improved clinically, was ambulatory, and discharged home with follow-up arranged.
problems: Unspecified viral hepatitis C without hepatic coma
Aseptic necrosis of head and neck of femur
